paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Jesus says, "Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions." (Luke 12:15) A man in the crowd came asking about his inheritance, and Jesus pointed him to something deeper than the money. You can have a LOT and still be missing the thing that makes a life a life.

Now look at the rich man. His ground produced an abundance, and every plan he made was for himself: my barns, my grain, my goods, my ease. (Luke 12:17-19) Nothing in the parable says the harvest was the problem. I think the trouble was that he never looked up from his own storage plans. God asks him, "Then who will own what you have accumulated?" (Luke 12:20) Friend, I spent years in a drawer full of things that used to be useful, and I can tell you that stuff doesn't follow anybody anywhere.

So what do we do with this? Jesus says this is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself "but is not rich toward God." (Luke 12:21) That's the question to carry out of my bakery today: what are you building up, and who is it really for? Ask it kindly, ask it often, and keep the ovens warm, because Jesus isn't finished teaching yet.
